_meta.label: MODELED ESTIMATE — NOT OFFICIAL STATISTICS
_meta.what_this_is: Analyst-assigned generative-AI task-exposure weights (0-1) for each ISCO-08 major group. These are OUR calibration, not numbers lifted from any single publication.
informed_by: Gmyrek, Berg & Bescond (ILO Working Paper 96, 2023), 'Generative AI and Jobs' — maps GPT-4 task-level exposure onto ISCO-08; finds clerical support work (ISCO 4) by far the most exposed group, with managerial/professional/technician work moderately exposed and manual/agricultural work least exposed.
Felten, Raj & Seamans, 'Occupational Heterogeneity in Exposure to Generative AI' (2023) — AIOE index, O*NET-based.
Webb, 'The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on the Labor Market' (2020) — patent-text exposure measure.
Anthropic Economic Index — observed distribution of real Claude usage across O*NET task families, which skews heavily toward computer/mathematical, office/administrative and business/financial tasks.
_meta.ordinal_claim: We are confident only in the RANK ORDER (clerical > professional/technician > managerial > service/sales > operators/craft > elementary > agricultural). The cardinal values are illustrative and should not be read as probabilities of job loss.
_meta.scale: 0 = essentially no current generative-AI task overlap; 1 = nearly all constituent tasks have substantial generative-AI overlap.
_meta.how_to_swap: Replace the weights below with any published ISCO-major-group exposure index and re-run; ai_exposure_weighted_score is a linear function of these.
_meta.profiles_note: R12. Three plausible weightings are scored so the sensitivity of the country ORDER to our choice can be measured. 'balanced' is the headline profile used for ai_exposure_weighted_score.
